s: Resolution: increased maxPoolSize to 25 immediately, upgraded Atlas to M10, added pool monitoring within one week.
Postmortem action items: increase pool to 50, add connection pool metrics to Grafana, schedule weekly k6 load tests.
Key lesson: load testing is not optional — a 20-minute k6 run with 50 concurrent users would have caught the pool ceiling before Black Friday.
Incident i-003: .env with JWT secret and credentials committed to git for 17 months, discovered during security audit for open-source preparation.
Timeline: .env committed Feb 2023, removed from working dir but not history, repo went internal in Jun 2023, discovered Jul 2024.
Exposed secrets: JWT_SECRET (32-char string), MongoDB Atlas connection string, PayPal API credentials — all rotated during remediation.
Impact assessment: no confirmed exploitation detected via git log analysis or MongoDB Atlas audit logs during the 17-month exposure window.
Root cause: .gitignore excluded only node_modules/ and build/, missing .env; no pre-commit hooks or secret scanning tools configured.
Remediation: rotated all secrets in order, used git-filter-repo to purge .env from all branches/tags, invalidated all JWT sessions.
Postmortem actions: added .env to .gitignore, installed git-secrets pre-commit hook, added GitHub secret scanning, updated onboarding docs.
Key lesson: .env belongs in .gitignore on day one without exception; project templates that don't include this are a security risk.
Index of all ProShop UI screens: public pages, checkout flow, user pages, and admin pages with links to individual documentation.
Admin orders screen: table listing all orders with ID, user, date, total, paid/delivered status, and details navigation button.
Admin product edit screen: form with name, price, image URL + file upload, brand, category, stock, description fields.
Admin products screen: paginated table with create/edit/delete actions for product catalog management.
Admin user edit screen: form to modify user name, email, and isAdmin checkbox with success redirect.
Admin users screen: table with ID, name, email (mailto), admin status, and edit/delete action buttons.
Cart screen: two-column layout with item list (quantity dropdown, delete) and summary card (subtotal, checkout button).
Home screen: paginated product grid with keyword search, top-rated carousel, responsive 1-4 column layout.
Login screen: centered form with email/password fields, submit button, error messages, and register link with redirect support.
Order screen: complete order details with shipping/payment info, PayPal button for unpaid orders, admin deliver button for paid.
Payment screen: checkout step 3 with radio button for PayPal/credit card, saves method to Redux, redirects to order review.
Place order screen: final checkout review with shipping, payment, items summary and auto-calculated prices including tax/shipping.
Product detail screen: product image, metadata, price, quantity selector, add-to-cart button, and review section with star ratings.
Profile screen: two-column layout with profile edit form (name, email, password) and order history table.
Register screen: form with name, email, password, confirm password fields; auto-login after successful registration.
Shipping screen: checkout step 2 with address, city, postal code, country form fields, saves to Redux cart state.
A/B testing runbook: complete guide for designing and executing statistically rigorous product experiments in proshop-mern.
Pre-test checklist: clear hypothesis, defined metrics (conversion, AOV, abandonment), calculated sample size, and success criteria.
Sample size calculator: formula for detecting 5% lift with 95% confidence and 80% statistical power.
A/B test code setup: create test document in MongoDB, assign users to variants via hash-based randomization.
Frontend variant rendering: use feature flag to conditionally render different checkout UI components based on assigned variant.
Analytics event tracking: log key events (page view, add to cart, checkout start, purchase) for both control and variant users.
Test execution: Phase 1 validate split (days 1-2), Phase 2 collect data (days 3-7), verify no errors in variant rendering.
Decision framework: Win (p<0.05, lift>3%) → rollout 100%; Inconclusive → extend or abandon; Loss → keep control variant.
Example A/B test results template: test ID, duration, sample size, conversion rates, p-value, and recommendation.
Reference links for A/B testing: chi-squared calculator, sample size calculator, and statistical testing resources.
Database seed and reset runbook: manage MongoDB state with sample data seeding, production resets, and backup procedures.
Local development workflows: fresh start after clone, reset between test runs, and seed with sample data commands.
Production reset warning: NEVER run data:destroy in production without explicit approval and verified backup.
Backup procedures: mongodump for full database backup, MongoDB Atlas automated snapshots, and restore commands.
Seed data: admin user (admin@example.com/123456), 8-10 sample products with images, empty orders collection.
Custom seeding guide: create custom seed files for specific test scenarios and add npm scripts for execution.
Production-like seeding: generate 1000+ products with varied attributes for staging and performance testing.
Database health monitoring: check database size, collection counts, and storage statistics via mongosh commands.
Seed troubleshooting: import hangs (MongoDB not running), seed succeeds but no products (wrong DB), duplicate key errors.
Deployment runbook: step-by-step Heroku production deployment with pre-flight checks, build process, and monitoring.
Heroku environment setup: create .env.production with Atlas connection string, JWT secret, PayPal credentials as config vars.
Deployment process: verify clean main branch, build frontend, push to Heroku, verify dyno start and frontend serving.
Rollback: Heroku releases command for instant rollback, or git-based revert if rollback command unavailable.
Post-deployment monitoring: check Heroku logs for errors, monitor dyno performance, verify API response and frontend loading.
Troubleshooting: H14 (missing Procfile), Application error (missing module), build failures (Node version mismatch).
Post-deployment: update CHANGELOG, git tag the release, notify team of deployment completion and any config changes.
Reference commands: git push heroku main, heroku logs --tail, heroku config, heroku releases, heroku rollback.
Feature flag toggle runbook: progressive canary deployment, kill switch for emergency disable, and rollout phase management.
Pre-rollout: implement both old and new code paths behind flag, test locally with flag enabled and disabled.
Rollout phases: internal testing (0→5%), canary beta (5→25%), expansion (25→50→100%) with monitoring at each stage.
Kill switch: instantly disable feature flag in MongoDB without code deployment, verify disabled via API check.
Incident example: new-search-filter caused P1 affecting 25% of users, killed in 5 minutes, root cause was MongoDB timeout.
Monitoring checklist during rollout: error rate (alert >1%), p95 latency (alert >2s), conversion rate, CPU/memory.
Post-rollout cleanup: keep flag as permanent kill switch or remove entirely with code cleanup after 24+ hours stability.
Reference commands for MongoDB feature flag operations: find, updateOne, aggregation for flag management.
Incident response runbook: structured 7-phase response from discovery through postmortem for production incidents.
Incident phases flow: discovery → declaration → triage → mitigation → resolution → verification → postmortem review.
Phase 1 discovery: incidents detected via monitoring alerts, user reports, or manual checks; declare incident with severity.
Phase 2 triage: assemble incident commander + lead engineer, assess severity, check recent deployments, identify affected systems.
Phase 3 mitigation: rollback recent deploy or use feature flag kill switch to stop user impact within 10-20 minutes.
Phase 4 resolution: identify and fix root cause (expired credentials, code bug, infrastructure issue) after mitigation.
Phase 5 verification: confirm error rates back to zero, API responses normal, frontend loading correctly after fix.
Phase 6 communication: regular Slack updates, stakeholder timeline, customer notification for outages over 5 minutes.
Phase 7 postmortem: blameless review within 24 hours, document timeline, root cause, action items with owners and deadlines.
Incident command roles: IC declares severity and owns communications, engineer lead investigates and deploys fixes.
Escalation contacts: on-call engineer, team lead, VP Engineering for severe incidents, reference commands for incident response.
Local setup runbook: bootstrap ProShop development environment on a fresh machine in 10-15 minutes with Docker for MongoDB.
Step-by-step setup: clone repo, install dependencies, start MongoDB Docker container, configure .env, seed database, run dev server.
Verify application: curl localhost:5001/api/products returns JSON array, open localhost:3000 for frontend, test login with seed accounts.
Common issues: port 5001 already in use (kill process or change PORT), MongoDB connection refused (start Docker container).
Command reference: npm run dev (backend+frontend), npm run server (backend only), npm run data:import (seed), npm run data:destroy (wipe).
Next steps after setup: explore backend routes, frontend components, read API docs, run the seed script, try creating an order.
Clean shutdown: npm run mongo:down stops MongoDB Docker container to prevent port conflicts on next startup.
